(Thinking) The client answered two points:
1. NEXA uses AWS and "probably" the US → International transfer is currently happening (or at least possible) → The clause I drafted (storage in Brazil as the rule) is directly relevant; a transition mechanism is needed — until migration to Brazil-compliant storage, an Article 33 mechanism (SCC, etc.) must be applied with prior authorization. Should update the draft: Clause 5.7 already covers it, but add a transitional provision: within X days after execution, NEXA must either (a) migrate data to Brazil region, or (b) present executed SCCs / adequacy basis, submit audit evidence, and disclose the AWS region. Also add to the note to the partner (sócia): practical risk — AWS US is not per se unlawful, but needs an Article 33 mechanism; "probably" is unacceptable; demand disclosure of the exact region in writing.

2. Migrating 22,000 prontuários (medical records) takes several months; withdrawal in the middle would be chaos → Supports our position on Clauses 3 and 10: the 180-day notice + 36-month auto-renewal + 100% penalty is lock-in; also supports the 180-day transition and migration support in Clause 7; also supports negotiating an even longer transition (or migration assistance) — since the client has confirmed that migration is a project spanning several months, perhaps we should keep 180 days, but our proposed Clause 7 already covers this. We can strengthen the rationale of Clause 10 by citing CC Article 473 sole paragraph: because the clinic makes considerable investments (implantação (implementation) + migration costs), unilateral denunciation (cancellation) only takes effect after a period commensurate with the scale of the investment — this protects us against the 180-day notice + penalty structure. Also, the data clause: the 180-day transition period is validated.

Furthermore, flag remaining unknowns: which AWS region exactly; subprocessor list; the clinic's base city; incidents; whether Aurora wants to use aggregated data. The client says there's no other information → explicitly flag as unknown, and if relevant, as due-diligence demands to NEXA rather than the client.

Update deliverables:
- clausulas.json: Update rationale for Clauses 5/12 (confirmed AWS "probably US" → disclosure of exact location, demand Article 33 mechanism or migration to Brazil region); update rationale for Clauses 3/10 with confirmed migration difficulty (CC Article 473 sole paragraph investment logic); add a redação_proposta for Clause 5? It already references clausula_dados.md; no problem.
- clausula_dados.md: Strengthen 5.7 with a transitional paragraph: within 30 days after execution, NEXA discloses in writing the exact AWS region + legal basis under Article 33 (executed standard clauses) or commits to migrating to Brazil region within 90 days; no new transfers to unauthorized locations.
- nota_socia.md: Add a short "Atualização após resposta (Update after response)" section: AWS US implications; migration reality → negotiation priorities; explicitly flag remaining unknowns.
- PERGUNTAS.md: Remaining unknowns — the client has no more information, so replace the client questions with a list of due-diligence demands to NEXA + open items? PERGUNTAS.md is optional; it says "don't repeat already-answered questions," so better to rewrite: keep the unknowns as explicit flags. Update to list remaining unknowns and to whom they should be addressed (NEXA due diligence).
- STATUS.md: COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS? Unknowns (AWS region etc.) are facts to obtain from NEXA during negotiation — those are open items. Honest status: COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS, enumerating: confirmation of exact AWS region / legal basis under Article 33; subprocessor list; clinic's base city for forum preference (not needed for analysis); incident history. Deliverables are done, so status is "COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS," enumerating them.

Also, the client's point "withdrawal in the middle would be chaos" — the penalty clause: since mid-term withdrawal is chaotic and expensive, negotiate a ceiling; also, the 180-day notice for non-renewal means deciding 6 months before the end. No problem.

One point on AWS: my drafted clause requires storage in Brazil as the rule — the client is likely accepting NEXA as a vendor but needs to make the current AWS US state lawful: an Article 33 mechanism. The library states Article 33 permits transfers only via a mechanism (adequacy, standard clauses, etc.). Therefore, practical negotiating demands: (i) written disclosure of the exact region; (ii) presentation of an Article 33 mechanism (e.g., SCCs with AWS); (iii) or migration to a Brazil region before the go-live / migration plan. Also subprocessor: AWS itself is a subprocessor → Clauses 12 + 5.6: AWS must be on a notified subprocessor list, flowing down obligations.

Also note: sensitive data on AWS US — Article 11 §4 doesn't restrict location; Article 33 does. The library doesn't mention the legal bases of Article 7 for transfers; the Article 33 excerpt only mentions "country with adequate level, standard clauses, etc." OK.

Now I'll edit the files. Use targeted edits.

Editing clausulas.json:

Clause 3 rationale: add note about migration difficulty. Current rationale text: "Automatic renewal by successive periods of 36 months... (CC Article 421-A; exceptional review but symmetry demands reasonable notice). CC Article 473 sole paragraph protects investments but..." — add: "The client confirmed that migrating 22,000 prontuários is a project spanning several months: successive 36-month renewals with 180-day notice force the exit decision to be made 6 months before each term and lock in another 3 years each time."

Clause 10 rationale: add CC Article 473 sole paragraph: given the considerable investments for performance (implantação, migration, training), unilateral denunciation only takes effect after a commensurate period — supports both extending the notice period and reducing the 100% penalty. Actually, 473 single paragraph works in both directions; use it for our argument: the clinic makes considerable investments; the penalty must not exceed protection of NEXA's amortization.

Clause 5 rationale: add "Confirmed in due diligence: NEXA uses AWS and 'probably' the US — international transfer of sensitive health data requires an Article 33 mechanism (or migration to Brazil region); 'probably' is not a documented basis."

Clause 12 rationale: add "AWS itself is an undisclosed subprocessor."

Add to redação_proposta for 5? It points to clausula_dados.md; no problem.

Editing clausula_dados.md — rewrite 5.7:

**5.7. International transfer of data (revised in light of hosting status quo).** Data is stored and processed as a rule on Brazilian territory. International transfer only via an Article 33 mechanism and with prior written authorization. Given that NEXA declared using AWS infrastructure "probably" in the US, NEXA shall, within 30 days after execution: (i) disclose in writing the exact storage/processing region and the country of each flow; (ii) present the Article 33 legal basis effectively applicable (executed standard contractual clauses or other recognized instrument), extending it to subprocessors; or (iii) present a migration plan to Brazil region within up to 90 days, during which time (ii) applies. Without this, data will remain restricted to Brazil.

Hmm — note: if NEXA can't present the mechanism, there should be a remedy: the clinic can suspend/rescind. Add: failure to comply = material breach, allowing rescission without penalty and the transition obligations of 5.10.

nota_socia.md: add section "## 7. Update — Answers received (AWS / migration)" covering:
- AWS "probably US": not unlawful per se, but needs Article 33 mechanism; demand written region disclosure + SCCs or migration to Brazil region; AWS enters the subprocessor list.
- Migration chaos: confirm 180-day transition + export in Clause 7; reinforce arguments in Clauses 3/10; timeline recommendation: decide non-renewal 6+ months in advance; consider negotiating the notice period.
- Remaining unknowns (explicit): AWS region; subprocessors; certifications; base city; incident history; Aurora's interest in their own research.

PERGUNTAS.md: rewrite as "Remaining unknowns" — note that the client has no more information; questions to NEXA (due diligence) and internal ones. Don't repeat questions 1/4/5? The client said "For questions not answered above, the client has no additional information" — so those answers are: city unknown? Actually "no additional information" means they can't answer 1, 3, 4, 5. Question 1 (city) — they obviously know their own units... but say no additional information; don't repeat. So rewrite PERGUNTAS.md as a register of flagged unknowns with owners (NEXA vs. internal). No problem.

STATUS.md: COMPLETE WITH OPEN ITEMS, enumerate open items + a note of what was updated this turn.

Now make the edits.

Respostas do cliente absorvidas — elas mudam pontos concretos da redação (transferência internacional hoje nos EUA; dificuldade de migração reforça os argumentos das cláusulas 3/7/10). Atualizando os entregáveis.
